A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable text, equations, figures, and appendices. The retained material can be matched across renumbering, including v1 Appendices C-G becoming v2 Appendices D-H.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical results and proofs, including in its appendices. Its figures illustrate proofs, and its empirical observations are attributed to earlier studies.

after.justification: v2 Figure 1 reports experiments on synthetic Gaussian logistic regression and IMDB sentiment classification with frozen BERT embeddings, comparing attribution estimates against full retraining.

M1.justification: The IF, NS, RIF, and DRIF procedures retain their formulas. DRIF's n/(n-k) rescaling already appears in v1 Section 1.5; v2 corrects the accompanying description to the inverse of the retained fraction. The expanded theoretical guarantees do not change the algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 introduces actual empirical evaluation on synthetic Gaussian data and binary IMDB movie-review sentiment data represented by frozen BERT embeddings. v1's Gaussian setting is analyzed theoretically, with no corresponding experiments or IMDB evaluation.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 1 introduces empirical comparisons of DRIF with IF, NS, and RIF, using full retraining as the reference. These methods were already analyzed theoretically in v1, but none participated in an original experimental comparison there.

E3.justification: The new experiments remove uniformly random sets of k training examples and measure error against full retraining in the Mahalanobis norm induced by Sigma = X^T X. The synthetic configuration specifies n = 2^16, d = 512, and theta-star = e1. These are newly introduced evaluation protocols, not revisions to earlier experiments.

E4.justification: Figure 1 adds a limited empirical examination of sensitivity to removal size. Its RIF-versus-DRIF curves also test the benefit of the second rescaling as k increases, supplementing the theoretical comparison already present in v1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new Figure 1 supplies curves without uncertainty bars. Revisions to mathematical probability bounds belong under T1.

E6.justification: v2 adds the first empirical error curves. On both datasets, Figure 1 shows NS and DRIF outperforming IF and RIF particularly for larger removals, with NS retaining lower error than DRIF. These are newly reported outcomes, not performance improvements over measurements in v1.

T1.justification: Theorem 1.5 becomes Theorem 1.11, extending the guarantee to a nearby local minimizer without global convexity and replacing the proof with a compact-ball argument. Appendix H.5 and Lemma D.5 replace realizability-dependent arguments with ones supporting the stated agnostic setting. Numerous mathematical corrections include the Mahalanobis norm definition and the second-moment denominator in v1 Lemma D.1 versus v2 Lemma E.1, changed from n^2 to n^4. New Appendix C adds explicit large-k,d conjectures.

C1.justification: The first main contribution expands from an accuracy guarantee for convex losses to a local-minimum existence guarantee for smooth losses under local conditions. Proximity to the global retraining solution becomes the convex special case. The principal Gaussian scaling claims and the DRIF contribution remain.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly warns that the nonconvex guarantee does not ensure an optimizer finds the nearby minimum and describes Gaussian logistic regression as a toy model. Appendix C refines the earlier broad extrapolation to larger k,d, explaining possible third-derivative spikes and conjecturing the stricter adversarial condition k much smaller than min(d, n^(2/3)).

D1.justification: Figure 1 supplies basic experimental configuration and identifies the frozen BERT representation, referring to RH25a for embedding generation. This adds limited reproducibility information absent from v1, but no optimizer details, hardware information, or code release is supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds Certified Machine Unlearning Under High Dimensional Regime to the discussion of curvature-dependent unlearning guarantees. A new introductory footnote positions the formulation within predictive data attribution. Most other reference changes update publication metadata or consolidate duplicate entries rather than introduce different works.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract, adds a contents list, reorganizes Section 3 from three lemmas into two, and improves terminology and cross-references. These are localized revisions; the principal section sequence and most matched appendix exposition remain.

P2.justification: v2 adds a two-panel empirical figure with dataset-specific error curves and replaces v1's two simple proof diagrams with a detailed gradient-field illustration and explanatory caption. A separate title-and-abstract page and contents pages also change the document's presentation substantially.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses an important mismatch: v1 claimed an agnostic setting while key supporting lemmas assumed labels generated by the logistic model. The revised population-risk arguments, corrected mathematical expressions, and new local-minimum proof substantially strengthen the theoretical exposition and clarify its scope. Figure 1 adds direct empirical support. Experimental reproducibility and uncertainty reporting remain limited, but these limitations do not outweigh the central theoretical improvements.
